events.title: Elasticsearch released
events.summary: Shay Banon open-sourced Elasticsearch on February 8, 2010 — a distributed search and analytics engine with a JSON HTTP API.
events.about: Elasticsearch indexes documents in near real time and queries them with full-text search, filters, and aggregations. The ELK stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) became the default for log analytics and observability. Example: index millions of JSON log lines and search by `@timestamp`, status code, and free text in milliseconds.

narrative.whyChosen: Elasticsearch made Lucene-scale search accessible over HTTP with horizontal sharding.
narrative.whyImportant: It powered log analytics, site search, and security SIEM pipelines across the industry.
narrative.problemSolved: Building distributed full-text search required deep Lucene expertise; teams needed a batteries-included cluster.

events.title: Gunicorn first released
events.summary: Benoit Chesneau released Gunicorn on February 20, 2010 — a pre-fork WSGI HTTP server for Python web applications.
events.about: Gunicorn runs Django, Flask, and other WSGI apps behind nginx or a load balancer — worker processes handle requests while a master manages lifecycle. It ported Ruby's Unicorn model to Python with simple configuration. Example: `gunicorn myapp.wsgi:application --workers 4` serves a Django API on port 8000.

narrative.whyChosen: Gunicorn became the default production WSGI server for Python web frameworks.
narrative.whyImportant: It made deploying Python apps behind nginx a standard, well-understood pattern.
narrative.problemSolved: Python's built-in development server was not safe or performant for production traffic.
